name: Lola Vidal
life: “I still remember a route nobody knew ended at my cousin's house.” On Sunday, near the blocks below Foundry Lofts, Lola checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I use the linen round to keep an eye on three houses. The shirts make it look like honest nosiness.
appearance: Lola has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones. Look for a blunt cut just below the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a sand-colored linen shirt with a train token tied to a zipper pull. In conversation Lola rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Lola has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Lola can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To keep the linen route as an ordinary way of checking in.
family: Valentina Jiang is Lola’s cousin raised in the same household. Lola makes room at the table. Valentina brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The returned daughter*, Valentina says, “I heard her say enough in the hallway. I walked her out and saved the father's letter for a day she chooses.”
connections: Briar Patel. Borrowing a court shirt depends on knowing the person who actually runs the linen round.

reactions.situation: A staff supervisor demands the stranger's laundry back
reactions.response: Lola checks with the shirt's owner before handing it over to anyone else.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Lola asks the nearest shop worker to stay too, then talks about ordinary things until the child can explain who is late.
